$schema_description: Course Study App — Production Lecture Exam Additions Template. Defines past exam questions & verified model answers mapped to specific lecture slides across any course. Slide titles, sections, and deck metadata are defined centrally in slides_index.json and inherited automatically — do NOT repeat them here. All textual fields support full Markdown and LaTeX math ($inline$ or $$display$$ with double-escaped '\\'). The first slide entry below provides field-by-field instructions; subsequent entries show real examples.

_file_naming_and_placement.rule: Use a consistent lecture prefix matching the literature and lab addition files for this lecture (e.g., 'L1_literature.json', 'L1_exams.json', and 'L1_labs.json' all sit inside 'Code/src/data/lecture_additions/').

markdown_and_latex_support.note: ALL TEXTUAL FIELDS SUPPORT FULL GITHUB-FLAVORED MARKDOWN AND KATEX MATH ($inline$ or $$display$$).
markdown_and_latex_support.mandatory_json_backslash_rule: CRITICAL: In JSON strings, the backslash '\' is the JSON escape character. Every LaTeX command MUST use double backslashes '\\'. For example, write '$\alpha$', '$\text{ms}$', '$$\frac{a}{b}$$', and '$O(M \times N)$'. Never write unescaped '\t' or '\f'. Escape literal dollar signs in prose as \$.
markdown_and_latex_support.code_and_math_rules: Use backticks (`$var`) exclusively for code, shell syntax, packet headers, and script variables; use dollar signs ($math$) exclusively for LaTeX math (never nest backticks in math). Never output raw HTML/MathML tags like <span class='katex'> or <math>. Escape literal dollar signs in prose as \$.

lecture_id: INSTRUCTION: Unique identifier string matching an 'id' from slides_index.json (e.g. 'lectures-module-1', 'l1-crypto-intro'). Deck title, document filename, and slide titles are resolved automatically from slides_index.json.

slides._comment: SCHEMA & FIELD INSTRUCTIONS: Slide exam addition schema definition. Slide title and section are inherited automatically from slides_index.json.

questions._comment: TEMPLATE 1A: RELATED MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTION (Field instructions for multiple choice exam question answerable from this slide)

alternatives.is_correct: INSTRUCTION: A strict boolean (true if the alternative statement is correct according to the exam key, false if it is incorrect). Do not use strings 'true' or 'false'.
alternatives.lecture_explanation: MARKDOWN FIELD: Technical explanation justifying WHY the statement is True or False. Supports **bold**, `code`, bullet points (- item), and KaTeX math ($...$ or $$...$$ with double-escaped '\\'). slides._comment: EXAMPLE 1: CONCRETE SLIDE WITH RELATED MULTIPLE CHOICE EXAM QUESTION

questions.question: Consider evaluating two alternative cache replacement policies (Policy A vs. Policy B) under identical benchmark workloads. Which of the following statements regarding paired observations is correct?

alternatives.text: Paired observations eliminate workload-induced variance by computing differences $D_i = A_i - B_i$ across identical benchmark workloads.
alternatives.lecture_explanation: When both alternatives are subjected to identical workloads $W_i$, pairing tests the differences $D_i = A_i - B_i$. This cancels out the variance introduced by fluctuations in workload complexity, narrowing the confidence interval compared to an unpaired $t$-test.
alternatives.RR_addition: Jain (Section 13.2) emphasizes that pairing isolates the treatment effect from environmental heterogeneity, reducing sample requirements by up to $5\times$.

alternatives.text: An unpaired two-sample $t$-test is always statistically superior because it provides more degrees of freedom ($2n - 2$ vs. $n - 1$).
alternatives.lecture_explanation: Although an unpaired test has $2n - 2$ degrees of freedom compared to $n - 1$ for a paired test, this slight gain in degrees of freedom is vastly outweighed by the massive increase in sample variance if between-workload variance is large.

abbreviations.phrase: Analysis of Variance (statistical technique for comparing means)

slides._comment: EXAMPLE 2: CONCRETE SLIDE WITH RELATED WRITTEN EXAM QUESTION

questions.context: A network simulation model was developed in NS-2 to analyze end-to-end packet delay across a congested router bottleneck.

sub_questions.label: a
sub_questions.question: Explain the difference between model verification and model validation in simulation study methodology.
sub_questions.lecture_explanation: **Model Verification** ensures the conceptual simulation model is correctly implemented in software/code (debugging: 'building the model right'). **Model Validation** ensures the simulation model accurately reflects the physical real-world system behavior (fidelity: 'building the right model').
sub_questions.RR_addition: According to Banks et al. (Chapter 10), validation requires face validation, input-output transformation testing, and comparison against historical physical traces using calibration metrics like Theil's inequality coefficient.

sub_questions.label: b
sub_questions.question: State two empirical techniques used to detect the end of the transient warmup phase in discrete-event simulation output.
sub_questions.lecture_explanation:
1. **Welch's Moving Average Procedure**: Averaging across multiple independent replications and plotting moving averages over window $w$ to visually locate the point where the metric curve flattens.
2. **Batch Means Heuristic**: Discarding initial deletion period $d$ until autocorrelation between successive batch means drops below threshold $\rho < 0.05$.
